notes: Wall clock 2.62h against an estimate of 2.5h looks near-exact, and that is a coincidence worth not believing. Active engineering was ~1.1h, a 2.3x over-estimate; the remaining ~1.5h was blocked on the gh OAuth token lacking the workflow scope, which needed a browser login the agent could not perform. Two errors in opposite directions happened to cancel. Recorded as partial for exactly that reason: scoring this as an accurate prediction would teach the calibrator the wrong lesson twice over.

Under-estimated by ~2.1x on the measure the estimate was stated in: 2.0h of active engineering predicted, ~4.2h spent. Active time is the sum of four working windows bounded by commit timestamps, each extended backwards by the reading that preceded its first commit; it is an estimate of an estimate's error and nothing here measures keystrokes. The blocked figure is not usefully comparable to OUT-0001's: the phase ran across four sessions ended by credit exhaustion, so the 68.5h is elapsed time containing nights rather than measured waiting, recorded only so the wall clock reconciles. Compare active against active. Where the estimate went wrong is legible: it priced the records and the schema, which cost about what was predicted, and did not price the four store test modules that make them trustworthy - roughly 1,700 lines and over half the engineering. Direction is the opposite of OUT-0001's, in a different work class, at n=1 each: exactly the shape of data a human over-reads and BiasDetective refuses to answer on below n=5.

Under-estimated by ~1.24x on the measure the estimate was stated in: 4.5h of active engineering predicted, ~5.6h spent. Same methodology as OUT-0002 and the same caveat - three working windows bounded by commit timestamps (1.25h, 2.35h, 2.0h), each extended backwards by the work that preceded its first commit, so this is an estimate of an estimate's error and nothing here measures keystrokes. The third window's lead-in is the least certain figure in the record because it precedes any commit: synthesis.py and its 58 tests were written before the first commit of that session. Blocked time is elapsed time containing a night, recorded only so the wall clock reconciles; compare active against active. Scored close rather than exact because the scope was not the scope that was priced, and it moved in both directions. Not built: the bounded repair loop named in the estimate's subject, now in BACKLOG.md with its reason - its shape is decided by what the first agents actually get back, and writing it now would be guessing at a failure distribution nobody has measured. Substituted: the per-agent mock response library for the five named agents became a schema-driven synthesiser that names no agent at all, which covers those five and every later one, and which is a better answer to the same requirement rather than a cheaper one. Built beyond the estimate: the boundary test, the provider factory, RecordingAnthropicProvider, and doctor making a real offline call. Also cheaper than priced: the estimate included two ADRs that turned out to already exist, written in Phase 0. The scope correction OUT-0002 asked for worked. EST-0003 priced roughly 2,200 production lines and roughly 3,000 test lines as line items; the actual is 2,246 production and 2,566 test - the production figure is close to exact, and the test figure is short by about the repair loop that was not built. That is the first estimate in this corpus whose conditions can be checked against the artifact rather than argued about. Third work class, third direction of error at n=1 each: over 2.3x, under 2.1x, under 1.24x. Still below BiasDetective's threshold, and still not a reason to correct EST-0004.
